1	# Entire Activity Design
2	
3	Date: 2026-04-15
4	
5	## Summary
6	
7	`Entire activity` is a new read-only product surface for understanding work captured by Entire over time.
8	
9	It is centered on:
10	
11	- sessions as the primary unit of work
12	- checkpoints as the evidence trail inside a session
13	- repo, time, and agent as first-class grouping dimensions
14	
15	This is not a sprint tool and should not use sprint language. It is an Entire-native activity layer over existing session, checkpoint, transcript, and commit-linkage data.
16	
17	## Goals
18	
19	- Show what happened today and across selectable time ranges.
20	- Make checkpoint and session activity easy to scan quickly.
21	- Surface useful, defensible insights instead of generic churn metrics.
22	- Support history, heatmap, repo, and agent views in the initial version.
23	- Support interactive TUI and static output in the initial version.
24	- Use only metrics that are either directly available now or safely derivable from existing data.
25	
26	## Non-Goals
27	
28	- No productivity score.
29	- No “most modified files” leaderboard as a primary signal.
30	- No sprint framing.
31	- No LLM-generated prose as a foundational feature.
32	- No claims of labor time or focus time beyond actual timestamp spans.
33	
34	## Product Definition
35	
36	`Entire activity` answers:
37	
38	- what happened
39	- when it happened
40	- where it happened
41	- what kind of work it was
42	- which agents and models were involved
43	- which checkpoints linked to commits
44	- what should likely be resumed
45	
46	## Views
47	
48	The full v1 surface includes:
49	
50	- `today`
51	- `range`
52	- `history`
53	- `agents`
54	- `repos`
55	- `report`
56	- session and checkpoint drill-down
57	
58	Profiles only change defaults and emphasis:
59	
60	- `personal`
61	- `team`
62	- `observability`
63	
64	## Command Surface
65	
66	```bash
67	entire activity
68	entire activity today
69	entire activity range --last 7d
70	entire activity range --from 2026-04-01 --to 2026-04-15
71	entire activity history
72	entire activity agents
73	entire activity repos
74	entire activity report --template daily --format markdown
75	```
76	
77	Shared flags:
78	
79	```bash
80	--repo current|owner/name|all
81	--profile personal|team|observability
82	--from YYYY-MM-DD
83	--to YYYY-MM-DD
84	--last 7d|14d|30d
85	--group-by repo|day|agent
86	--view cards|table
87	--json
88	```
89	
90	Notes:
91	
92	- `entire activity` should open the TUI by default.
93	- `--repo all` is a scoped v1 goal only if repo discovery/indexing is implemented. It is not available from current repo-local data alone.
94	- All subcommands must support static terminal output and JSON output.
95	
96	## Data Truth Table
97	
98	The spec only relies on metrics in these buckets.
99	
100	### Directly Available Now
101	
102	From session state and committed checkpoint metadata, the CLI already has:
103	
104	- session ID
105	- checkpoint ID
106	- session started/ended timestamps
107	- checkpoint timestamps
108	- last interaction timestamp
109	- session phase
110	- session checkpoint count
111	- task checkpoint flag and tool use ID
112	- files touched
113	- agent type
114	- model name
115	- token usage where available
116	- turn IDs
117	- prompt text / last prompt
118	- worktree path and worktree ID
119	- checkpoint/session multi-session metadata
120	- attribution metadata
121	- session hook metrics for some agents:
122	  - duration
123	  - turn count
124	  - context tokens
125	  - context window size
126	
127	### Derivable From Existing Data
128	
129	The following are safe to compute from current data:
130	
131	- session span from timestamps
132	- checkpoints per session
133	- checkpoint density
134	- median checkpoint gap
135	- sessions/day
136	- checkpoints/day
137	- active day count
138	- streaks
139	- heatmap cells
140	- resume-after-gap badge
141	- focus areas from path clustering on `files_touched`
142	- linked commit count and linked commit rate via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer lookup
143	- commit-linked vs exploratory-only split
144	- mode labels from deterministic rules over:
145	  - timestamps
146	  - checkpoint counts
147	  - task checkpoint share
148	  - linked commits
149	  - focus area concentration
150	  - transcript tool-use structure when available
151	
152	### Conditional Metrics
153	
154	These are valid, but must be rendered as conditional:
155	
156	- tokens: only when transcript or hook-derived token extraction is available
157	- session duration/turn/context metrics: only for agents that report them
158	- transcript-derived tool profile metrics: only when transcript tool-use events are available
159	
160	### Not Currently Universal
161	
162	These must not be presented as already available everywhere:
163	
164	- cross-repo discovery for `--repo all`
165	- universal explicit session duration
166	- universal tool profile across all agents
167	- LLM-written narrative summaries
168	
169	## Core Data Model
170	
171	### ActivitySession
172	
173	- repo
174	- session ID
175	- branch when available
176	- worktree ID
177	- started at
178	- ended at
179	- last interaction at
180	- span minutes
181	- checkpoint count
182	- task checkpoint count
183	- linked commit count
184	- checkpoints
185	- agents used
186	- models used
187	- focus areas
188	- primary label
189	- confidence
190	- reasons
191	- badges
192	- token totals
193	- is active
194	- is resumable
195	
196	### ActivityCheckpoint
197	
198	- repo
199	- session ID
200	- checkpoint ID
201	- timestamp
202	- is task checkpoint
203	- tool use ID
204	- agent
205	- model
206	- focus areas
207	- linked commit SHA
208	- token usage
209	- turn ID
210	- badges
211	
212	### ActivityDay
213	
214	- date
215	- repos
216	- sessions
217	- checkpoints
218	- task checkpoints
219	- linked commits
220	- token totals
221	- mode counts
222	- focus area counts
223	- resume count
224	
225	### ActivityRangeSummary
226	
227	- from
228	- to
229	- repos touched
230	- sessions
231	- checkpoints
232	- task checkpoints
233	- linked commits
234	- active days
235	- tokens
236	- mode counts
237	- focus area counts
238	- agent counts
239	- model counts
240	- repo summaries
241	- top sessions
242	
243	### ActivityRepoSummary
244	
245	- repo
246	- sessions
247	- checkpoints
248	- linked commits
249	- linked commit rate
250	- focus areas
251	- mode counts
252	- agents used
253	- top sessions
254	
255	### ActivityAgentSummary
256	
257	- agent
258	- models
259	- sessions
260	- checkpoints
261	- task checkpoint rate
262	- checkpoint density
263	- linked commit rate
264	- mode counts
265	- focus areas
266	- token totals
267	- outlier sessions
268	
269	## Work-Mode Labels
270	
271	Primary labels:
272	
273	- `build`
274	- `fix`
275	- `review`
276	- `refactor`
277	- `mixed`
278	
279	Badges:
280	
281	- `resumed`
282	- `linked commit`
283	- `delegated`
284	- `multi-repo`
285	
286	Removed from primary labels:
287	
288	- `agent-heavy`
289	- `commit-heavy`
290	- `explore`
291	
292	Reason:
293	
294	- they are either too vague or safer as badges/secondary metrics than as a primary work-mode label.
295	
296	## Deterministic Classification Rules
297	
298	Each session gets:
299	
300	- `primary_label`
301	- `confidence`
302	- `reasons[]`
303	- `badges[]`
304	
305	The classifier must be deterministic and conservative.
306	
307	### Input Features
308	
309	- checkpoint count
310	- task checkpoint share
311	- linked commit count
312	- focus area concentration
313	- longest consecutive focus area run
314	- session span minutes
315	- median checkpoint gap minutes
316	- focus area count
317	- resume gap hours
318	- transcript tool category shares when available
319	- retry cycle count when available
320	- stalled cycle count when available
321	- label keyword hits
322	- rename/move count when available
323	
324	### Confidence Gate
325	
326	Assign a primary label only if:
327	
328	- winning score `>= 6`
329	- winning score leads runner-up by `>= 2`
330	- winning label has at least 2 non-keyword signals
331	
332	Otherwise:
333	
334	- `primary_label = mixed`
335	
336	### Exact Label Rules
337	
338	#### `fix`
339	
340	Gate:
341	
342	- `checkpoint_count >= 2`
343	- and one of:
344	  - `retry_cycles >= 2`
345	  - `focus_area_run_max >= 3`
346	  - `stalled_cycles >= 1` and fix keywords
347	
348	Score:
349	
350	- `+3` if `retry_cycles >= 2`
351	- `+2` if `focus_area_concentration >= 0.60`
352	- `+2` if `focus_area_run_max >= 3`
353	- `+1` if `median_checkpoint_gap_min <= 12`
354	- `+1` if fix keywords appear
355	- `+1` if linked commit exists after repeated same-area work
356	
357	#### `build`
358	
359	Gate:
360	
361	- `checkpoint_count >= 2`
362	- and one of:
363	  - `tool_fileops_share >= 0.50`
364	  - `linked_commit_count >= 1`
365	
366	Score:
367	
368	- `+2` if `tool_fileops_share >= 0.50`
369	- `+2` if `linked_commit_count >= 1`
370	- `+1` if `session_span_min >= 20`
371	- `+1` if `0.40 <= focus_area_concentration < 0.80`
372	- `+1` if `1 <= focus_area_count <= 3`
373	- `+1` if build keywords appear
374	- `-2` if `retry_cycles >= 2`
375	
376	#### `review`
377	
378	Gate:
379	
380	- `task_checkpoint_share >= 0.40`
381	- or `tool_agent_share >= 0.30` and review keywords
382	
383	Score:
384	
385	- `+3` if `task_checkpoint_share >= 0.50`
386	- `+2` if review keywords appear
387	- `+1` if `focus_area_count >= 2`
388	- `+1` if `tool_fileops_share < 0.40`
389	- `+1` if `linked_commit_count == 0`
390	
391	#### `refactor`
392	
393	Gate:
394	
395	- refactor keywords
396	- and one of:
397	  - `rename_move_count >= 1`
398	  - `focus_area_count >= 2`
399	  - `linked_commit_count >= 1`
400	
401	Score:
402	
403	- `+4` if refactor keywords appear
404	- `+2` if `rename_move_count >= 1`
405	- `+1` if `focus_area_count >= 2`
406	- `+1` if `linked_commit_count >= 1`
407	
408	#### `mixed`
409	
410	Default when no label clears the gate.
411	
412	### Range-Level Mode Rendering
413	
414	Never claim a dominant mode for a range unless:
415	
416	- top mode share `>= 0.55`
417	- and top mode leads second mode by `>= 0.15`
418	
419	Otherwise render:
420	
421	- `mixed activity`
422	
423	Preferred presentation:
424	
425	- `Modes: build 4 · fix 3 · mixed 2`
426	
427	Avoid:
428	
429	- “you spent this week debugging”
430	
431	unless the range-level evidence truly supports it.
432	
433	## Focus Areas
434	
435	Focus areas are a required product signal.
436	
437	### Rule Source
438	
439	Resolution order:
440	
441	1. repo-local config
442	2. built-in rules
443	3. fallback path clustering
444	
445	Repo-local config file:
446	
447	- `.entire/activity_areas.json`
448	
449	Schema:
450	
451	```json
452	{
453	  "version": 1,
454	  "areas": [
455	    {
456	      "match": "cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/**",
457	      "label": "checkpoint storage",
458	      "priority": 100
459	    }
460	  ]
461	}
462	```
463	
464	### Matching Rules
465	
466	- highest priority wins
467	- if equal priority, longest match wins
468	- if no explicit rule matches, fallback to the first meaningful repo-relative directory boundary
469	
470	### Built-In Default Rules For This Repo
471	
472	- `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/**` -> `checkpoint storage`
473	- `cmd/entire/cli/session/**` -> `session state`
474	- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/**` -> `checkpoint strategy`
475	- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/**` -> `agent integrations`
476	- `cmd/entire/cli/search**` -> `search`
477	- `cmd/entire/cli/explain**` -> `explain`
478	- `cmd/entire/cli/status**` -> `status`
479	- `cmd/entire/cli/trace**` -> `trace`
480	- `cmd/entire/cli/hooks**` -> `hooks`
481	- `cmd/entire/cli/trail/**` -> `trail`
482	- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/**` -> `integration tests`
483	- `e2e/**` -> `e2e`
484	- `docs/architecture/**` -> `architecture docs`
485	- `docs/**` -> `docs`
486	
487	### Area Ranking
488	
489	Do not rank by file count.
490	
491	Session area score:
492	
493	- `4 * checkpoint_participation`
494	- `+1` if area appears in 2+ consecutive checkpoints
495	- `+1` if area appears in a linked-commit session
496	
497	Range area score:
498	
499	- `3 * session_participation`
500	- `3 * checkpoint_participation`
501	- `+1` if area appears across multiple repos when cross-repo scope exists
502	
503	Render only top 1-3 focus areas in summary surfaces.
504	
505	## TUI Layout
506	
507	The primary surface should be dashboard-first, not list-first.
508	
509	### Main Layout
510	
511	Top row:
512

514	- Checkpoints
515	- Linked Commits
516	- Repos

527

531	- checkpoint strip
532	- linked commit markers
533	- agent/model details
534

536	
537	- `1-5` switch views
538	- `[` / `]` move range preset
539	- `r` cycle repo filter
540	- `p` cycle profile
541	- `m` cycle heatmap metric
542	- arrow keys move selection
543	- `enter` toggle drill-down

545	- `g` cycle grouping
546	- `q` quit

550	Heatmap is in scope for v1.

562	- team: linked commits
563	- observability: checkpoints
564

567	- columns = days
568	- rows = weeks
569	- value = selected metric aggregated for the day

# Worktale: Product Overview

## Core Product
Worktale is a CLI tool that automatically tracks developer work by analyzing git commits across repositories. It generates searchable work logs with AI-generated summaries, activity streaks, and visual heatmaps—all stored locally without any cloud uploads.

## Three-Step Setup
Installation is streamlined: `npm install -g worktale`, initialize per repo with `worktale init`, then run `worktale digest` for daily summaries.

## Dashboard Views (Interactive TUI)

The interface offers three keyboard-navigable panels:

1. **Overview** - High-level metrics including commit count, lines added/removed, files changed, and estimated time spent
2. **Daily Log** - Chronological view of commits for a specific day with user notes and precise timestamps
3. **History** - Year-spanning visualization showing activity distribution across days

## Key Metrics Displayed
- **Streak counter** - Consecutive days with commits
- **Best streak record** - All-time longest active period
- **Activity heatmap** - Visual representation of commit frequency by day of week
- **Aggregate statistics** - Total commits, lines written, and days active across tracked period

## Information Architecture
The design emphasizes **actual engineering output** over estimation. It juxtaposes Jira's theoretical tickets against real commit history, positioning itself as a source-of-truth work record for standups, performance reviews, and personal momentum tracking.

All data uses local SQLite storage with zero network requests or telemetry.

content.text:
I've read the design doc, the Worktale and CodeBurn references, Alisha's merged hackweek PRs, and skimmed the existing CLI layout. Here's my review.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The plan's "Data Truth Table" (directly available / derivable / conditional / not universal) is the single most valuable structural choice in the doc — it's the same discipline that keeps `manual_commit` strategy honest about what's real vs derived, and it prevents v1 from promising metrics the agents don't actually report. Preserve it.
- `manual_commit_condensation.go` + the `entire/checkpoints/v1` tree at `<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/metadata.json` is the activity layer's primary input. That makes the proposed `activity` package a *read-only projection over committed checkpoints plus live session state* — no new storage, no new hooks, no branch writes. That's the right blast radius.
- Alisha's #1021 already built a classifier-adjacent feature pipeline server-side (`toolProfile`, `executionFeedback` thrashing, `bugProfile`, `architectureChanges`) off `transcript_stripped`. The plan's CLI classifier must either reuse or deliberately mirror that feature schema — otherwise a checkpoint's mode in `entire activity` and on the web app will disagree, which is worse than either answer alone.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Overall take

The plan is strong and unusually principled for a v1 design doc. The anti-sprint stance, the conservative `mixed`-as-default classifier, the explicit confidence gate, and the rule-based focus areas all feel like they came from someone who has watched generic dashboards fail. I'd green-light the direction.

The areas I'd push on are mostly about **scope fit** (does it answer the "my week" framing the user actually wants?), **alignment with the hackweek classifier work** (don't build two), and **the "now what?" question** (the plan is viewing, not actioning).

## What it gets right

1. **Sessions as the primitive, checkpoints as evidence.** This matches how the strategy package already models the world (`SessionState` + sharded `CheckpointSummary`). Anything else would force re-modeling.
2. **No sprint framing, no productivity score, no LLM prose in v1.** All three would be regressions. Keep them banned.
3. **Confidence gate + `mixed` fallback.** Labeling 40% of sessions as `mixed` is a feature, not a bug — it's what keeps the other labels meaningful.
4. **Focus-area rule engine with `.entire/activity_areas.json`.** Right place in the config hierarchy, explicit priority tiebreak, fallback to path clustering. This is the single feature most likely to determine whether users trust the tool or not — the built-ins for this repo are already sensible.
5. **Checkpoint linkage via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.** Maps 1:1 to the existing condensation pipeline; no new linkage mechanism to invent.

## The biggest gaps

### 1. Reuse Alisha's classifier features; don't fork

`classify.go`'s input features (`tool_fileops_share`, `tool_agent_share`, `retry_cycles`, `stalled_cycles`, `rename_move_count`) are exactly what PR #1021 computes server-side as `toolProfile` / `executionFeedback`. Two options:

- **(Preferred)** Extract the feature derivation into a shared package (Go port of the TS logic, or a shared schema) so CLI-local classification and backend `SessionReview` classification always agree on features, even if weights evolve independently. The plan should pick one implementation and cite it.
- **(Weaker)** Accept drift and render a "web summary may differ" note somewhere in the UI.

Without this, users will notice when the TUI says `build` and the web-app summary pill says `fix` — and that's the bug report that kills trust.

### 2. "Time spent debugging" needs a first-class aggregate

The user's framing ("how much time someone spent debugging") maps to `fix` but the range/history views show mode *counts* only. Add a **Time by Mode** panel at range/history level using `sum(session_span_minutes)` bucketed by `primary_label` — with an explicit caveat in the label ("time between first and last checkpoint, not focus time"). This directly answers what Alisha's team was exploring and what worktale-style tools imply but rarely deliver honestly.

### 3. "Now I have all these checkpoints, now what?" — this is viewing, not actioning

The plan has drill-down but no explicit verbs. Consider hotkeys / subcommands from any selected session or checkpoint:
- `R` → `entire resume <session-id>` (especially for sessions with no linked commit)
- `C` → suggest `entire` condense/commit flow when checkpoints are stacked and unlinked
- `X` → `entire explain <file:line>` pointing into the selected checkpoint's transcript
- `T` → `entire trace` / `entire search` with the selected session pre-filtered
- `D` → diff of files_touched at that checkpoint

Without verbs, "activity" is a reporting tool. With them, it's a dispatch hub — which fits the worktree name (`entire-dispatch-command`) and the user's actual need.

### 4. `--repo all` is listed as conditional for v1; it probably shouldn't be

"My day / my week" is almost always multi-repo for real users. If `--repo all` ships as a stub, `entire activity` becomes "activity in this one repo," which is a worse product than what either Worktale or CodeBurn already offers. Cheap path to v1 cross-repo:

- Maintain a small local index at `~/.entire/activity/repos.json` listing every repo where `entire enable` has run (append on enable, dedupe on read).
- Each entry points to the repo path; activity loader iterates, skipping missing paths.
- No indexing daemon, no cross-machine sync — just a pointer set.

This is maybe a half-day of work and it unlocks the actual framing the user asked for.

### 5. Privacy on prompts

`Data Truth Table` lists `prompt text / last prompt`. CLAUDE.md's privacy guidance bans logging user content. TUI rendering isn't logging, but `--json` output *is* effectively an export, and drill-downs that render prompts verbatim leak into screenshots. I'd default to redacted prompts (first 60 chars + hash) with `--with-prompts` to opt in, and keep prompts out of `--json` unless explicit.

### 6. Performance budget + caching

`entire activity history --last 90d` walks the metadata tree on `entire/checkpoints/v1` plus greps the user branch for `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. The plan acknowledges this but sets no budget. Propose:

- Sub-second for `today`, <3s for `range --last 7d`, <10s for `history` (90d).
- Cache at `.git/entire-activity-cache/<base-commit>.json`, invalidated when `entire/checkpoints/v1` or HEAD moves.
- Progress spinner in TUI, silent in `--json`.

### 7. Static output needs its own wireframe

All five wireframes are TUI-shaped panels. Static output (pipe, CI, `--json`-less plain text) will look nothing like those grids. Show one text-first layout (single column, flat cards) so the milestone 4 work has a target.

## Smaller suggestions

- **Collapse `today` into `range --last 1d`** (keep `today` as user-facing sugar, but share the one pipeline).
- **Add `week` / `month` sugar** alongside `range` — friendlier than typing `--last 7d`.
- **One-shot rate** (CodeBurn): % of edit→bash→edit retry cycles = 0. Cheap to derive, unique agent-quality signal, and it directly answers "is this agent actually helping me."
- **Tokens per linked commit** as a KPI, not just tokens total — that's an "agent insight" neither Worktale nor CodeBurn has, because neither knows which commits came from agent work.
- **Intra-day checkpoint density strip** on `today`: 24 cells across the top showing when checkpoints happened. A heatmap on `today` with only 1 row is wasted real estate.
- **Profiles** (personal/team/observability) are thin in the doc. Either spell out every delta each profile causes, or drop profiles until you have evidence for them. Today they look like premature abstraction.
- **Removed labels (`agent-heavy`, `commit-heavy`, `explore`)** — good call on dropping as primary. Consider keeping `agent-heavy` as a *badge* though; it's genuinely informative alongside `delegated`.
- **Fixture corpus for classifier precision targets** (milestone 6) should live at `cmd/entire/cli/activity/testdata/corpus/` with frozen `SessionState` + transcript JSONL inputs and expected-label YAML. Gate classifier PRs on precision CI.

## Questions before we start

1. **Is this command fully local, or does it fetch from api.entire.io when the user is logged in?** If authenticated, you could pull the already-generated `SessionReview` summaries from #1021 instead of re-deriving features locally. Big UX difference.
2. **Scope of v1 multi-repo** — OK with the `~/.entire/activity/repos.json` pointer set approach, or do you want `--repo all` truly punted?
3. **Time-spent framing** — do you want honest span-based time (first/last checkpoint) with caveats, or are you ok with "active minutes" estimated from checkpoint clustering (Worktale-style)? The former is defensible, the latter is more engaging but softer.
4. **Where does the classifier live?** CLI-only (duplicate of backend), or a shared feature-extraction library that both the CLI and `api/summary-queue.ts` call?
5. **Action hotkeys in v1** — can I slot resume/explain/trace/commit-compose affordances into milestone 5, or is v1 strictly read-only and actioning is v2?
6. **Worktree context** — you referenced both `entire-activity` and `entire-dispatch-command` worktrees. The plan lives in `dispatch-command`. Should I be working from `dispatch-command`, moving the doc into `entire-activity`, or treating these as the same feature under a name that hasn't settled yet?

Happy to go deeper on any of these — especially the classifier-alignment decision and the `--repo all` scope call, since those shape milestones 1-3.

content.text:
I found the pieces I needed. Important correction and some surprises:

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The api (entirehq/entire.io) already has `/:org/:repo/overview/commit-stats`, `/:org/:repo/overview/contributors`, and `/:org/:repo/overview/pr-stats` — per-day breakdowns with `with_checkpoint` vs `without_checkpoint` split, timezone-aware. This is almost exactly the plan's range/history data model, already live server-side.
- The server's canonical label taxonomy (`CHECKPOINT_LABELS` in `api/src/types.ts`) is **18 multi-label** values (`feature_build, bug_fix, refactor, performance, optimization, investigation, configuration, testing, deployment, recovery, planning, security_fix, documentation, migration, telemetry, observability, enhancement, dependencies`), max 3 per checkpoint. The plan's 5-label single-primary model **does not match** — this is the biggest correctness issue to reconcile.
- `ToolProfile` on the server is 6 categories (`shell, fileOps, search, mcp, agent, other`). The plan's `tool_fileops_share` / `tool_agent_share` features are shadows of this — the CLI should consume `ToolProfile` directly, not re-derive.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Answers to your six points

### 1. Not local — confirmed, and bigger than I thought

The api already runs a pipeline (`api/src/lib/checkpoint-analysis-pipeline.ts`, version `2026-04-10.v3`) that uses Anthropic's SDK to produce `CheckpointExtraction { labels, blocks }`, plus `ToolProfile`, plus thrashing/bug/architecture flags (Alisha's #1021). Results are stored as `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` in the db.

**Implication for `entire activity`:**
- CLI is a **thin client** over `api.entire.io` when logged in.
- New endpoints we'll need (some already partially exist):
  - `GET /activity/overview?since&until&timeZone&repos[]` (aggregate across repos the user has access to)
  - `GET /:org/:repo/overview/session-spans?since&until` (honest time = max(checkpoint_ts) − min(checkpoint_ts) per session; this isn't in the api today from what I saw)
  - `GET /:org/:repo/checkpoints/:id/analysis` — already exists via the review/extraction machinery
  - Existing `/overview/commit-stats` and `/overview/contributors` already cover the KPI row
- Offline / not-logged-in fallback: degraded local-only view using just committed-checkpoint metadata. The UI should clearly label the mode (e.g. `entire activity — offline, labels unavailable`).

**Plan change:** rewrite the "Data Truth Table" with three tiers — server-authoritative, local-authoritative, local-derivable — so readers know where each metric comes from.

### 2. `--repo all` — my recommendation

**Default to all repos the user has access to** (scoped by login). Not "all repos on disk." Specifically:
- Logged-in default: query `api.entire.io` for repos the user has read access to, show activity across all of them.
- `--repo current` narrows to the repo of `cwd`.
- `--repo owner/name` narrows to one named repo.
- `--repo local` shows only the current local repo without calling the api (for offline/privacy).

This avoids indexing `$HOME` for checkpoint branches (expensive, racy) and reuses the auth + repo-access model `checkRepoAccess` already implements. It also maps cleanly to how users think about "my week" — across repos, not across machines.

Per-repo breakdown is still a primary panel in the range/history views (the plan's `Repos` view and `Repo Cards` already do this). What I'd change in the plan: promote "multi-repo aggregation via api" from "conditional v1" to the default, and drop the "cross-repo discovery" line from the Risks section because it's solved by the api.

### 3. Honest time — align with FE

I searched for session duration / span logic on the api side and didn't find a first-class aggregate today. What exists:
- checkpoint timestamps in db
- PR stats with timezone support
- commit-stats with `DATE_FORMAT(rc.commit_date, '%Y-%m-%d')` daily bucketing

So honest time isn't *yet* computed on the backend. To avoid divergence, we should **add it server-side first**, not in the CLI. Proposal:
- Add `session_span_minutes = (last_checkpoint_ts - first_checkpoint_ts)` as a stored column or view, bucketed by `timeZone` query param.
- Expose via `/overview/session-spans?since&until&timeZone`.
- CLI and FE both consume it. One definition, zero drift.

Label it honestly in the UI: "Span (first → last checkpoint)," not "focus time" or "labor time." This matches the plan's anti-bullshit stance.

### 4. Shared classifier — confirmed, and it already lives server-side

The LLM-based `CheckpointExtraction` is the canonical classifier. It's multi-label, max 3, from the 18-label list above.

**Plan changes required:**
- Drop the deterministic 5-label primary-label classifier in `classify.go` / `classify_rules.go`. It will drift from the server and users will see different labels in TUI vs web.
- Replace with: fetch `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` from the api per checkpoint. Render `labels[]` (up to 3) as pills per session/checkpoint card.
- Keep local-only badges (`resumed`, `linked commit`, `delegated`, `multi-repo`) — these are cheap deterministic facts from local session state, not classifications. They don't need a server round-trip.
- For range-level summaries ("modes panel"), aggregate by summing label occurrences across checkpoints/sessions, and render exactly like `Modes: feature_build 4 · bug_fix 3 · refactor 2`. The same rendering rule from the plan still applies (don't claim a dominant mode unless top share ≥ 0.55 and lead ≥ 0.15).

Note the plan's label names (`build`/`fix`/`review`/`refactor`/`mixed`) are friendlier than the server's underscored IDs (`feature_build`/`bug_fix`/...). If you want the CLI to render friendlier labels, do it in a pure display-mapping layer — but keep the canonical IDs as the underlying data. That way we can unify display naming across CLI and FE later.

### 5. Real commands in drill-down — confirmed exact syntax

I read the actual cobra definitions in this repo. The real verbs are:
- `entire explain --checkpoint <id>` (detailed view)
- `entire explain --checkpoint <id> --generate` (generate AI summary — this exists)
- `entire explain --checkpoint <id> --full` (full transcript)
- `entire explain --session <session-id>` (filter by session)
- `entire explain --commit <sha>` (via commit)
- `entire resume <branch>` (not `<session-id>` — it takes a branch name and resumes that branch's session)
- `entire search <query>` (checkpoint semantic + keyword search)
- `entire sessions list`, `entire sessions info <session-id>`, `entire sessions stop [session-id]`
- `entire trail list`, `entire trail create`
- `entire trace` (hook perf)

So the drill-down panel in the plan should have an **Actions** footer listing real, copy-pasteable invocations. Example:

```text
┌ Drilldown: 11:20-12:01 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Session: 2026-04-15-abc...   Agent: Claude Code   Model: sonnet                │
│ Labels: feature_build, testing                                                 │
│ Badges: linked commit                                                          │
│                                                                                 │
│ 11:22  cp a1b2c3def456  hooks                  wrote files                     │
│ 11:34  cp b2c3d4e5f678  checkpoint strategy    linked commit abc123            │
│ 11:49  cp c3d4e5f67890  hooks                  final checkpoint                │
│                                                                                 │
│ Actions                                                                         │
│   entire explain --checkpoint b2c3d4e5f678                                     │
│   entire explain --checkpoint b2c3d4e5f678 --generate                          │
│   entire resume session-abc                                                    │
│   entire search "hooks"                                                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

(Note `entire resume` takes a *branch*, not a session id. I'd either add a session-id mode to `resume` as a small follow-up, or map `session → branch` in the drilldown before rendering.)

Hotkeys can still exist in TUI mode to `exec` these commands, but the underlying verbs are real, and users can also just type them.

### 6. Worktree — move to `entire-activity`

I'd move the design doc to the `entire-activity` worktree. Rationale:
- The branch is already named `entire-activity` (matches the command).
- `entire-dispatch-command` is a name that doesn't describe the v1 scope (dispatch/actioning is v2 per your point 5).
- Implementation will happen on the `entire-activity` branch anyway.

If you want, I can move the file and delete the `entire-dispatch-command` worktree — but say the word first since worktree deletion is the kind of shared-state thing I don't want to do without confirmation.

## Summary of plan changes I'd make before M1 starts

1. **Drop the CLI-side deterministic classifier.** Replace with api-fetched `StoredCheckpointAnalysis`. Multi-label, 18-value taxonomy, max 3 per checkpoint.
2. **Rewrite Data Truth Table** into three tiers: server-authoritative, local-authoritative, local-derivable.
3. **Promote `--repo all` to default** via api-backed repo access scoping. Drop `--repo all` from the Risks list.
4. **Move session-span computation to the api first,** expose via a new endpoint, then consume in CLI + FE. Label it "Span (first → last checkpoint)."
5. **Rename "Modes" panel labels** to match server taxonomy (or add a display-mapping layer that's unified across CLI + FE).
6. **Rework drill-down** to show real `entire ...` invocations as an Actions footer.
7. **Add an offline fallback** section to the plan spelling out what degrades (labels, cross-repo aggregation, AI summaries) when `entire login` hasn't been run.

Happy to make these edits to the design doc once you confirm:
- Move to `entire-activity` worktree?
- OK to replace the deterministic classifier section with an "api-consumes" section?
- OK to add the `/overview/session-spans` endpoint as a server-side precondition for v1?

content.text:
Important finding on #1 — the FE "Continuity" metric is not a real time measurement.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `frontend/.../useUserDashboardData.ts` computes `continuity.hours = max(checkpoint.steps) × 2 / 60` — a hardcoded 2-minutes-per-step estimate against the single checkpoint with the highest step count, not real timestamps. So "Peak session length 1.3h" is a derived heuristic, not measured session span.
- `strategy.ListSessionStates(ctx)` and `strategy.ListCheckpoints()` already expose `BaseCommit`, `StartedAt`, `LastInteractionAt`, `CheckpointCount`, and local `entire/checkpoints/v1` reads — all offline, all fast. The CLI already has honest-time primitives the FE doesn't use.
- The right architecture is **local-first with api as enrichment**, not api-first. Active/unpushed sessions only live locally, and `entire activity today` has to see those or it fails the primary use case.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## 1. Continuity metric — don't copy it, replace it

The FE formula:

```ts
continuity.hours = Math.max(...checkpoints.map(cp => cp.steps || 1)) * 2 / 60
```

It's `max(steps) × 2 min / 60`. Not a timestamp span. That 2-min coefficient is hardcoded and the metric is already somewhat honest-adjacent (it's labeled "Peak session length" but it's really "Peak step count × estimate").

Two recommendations:

**A) In the CLI, compute honest time locally and render both.** The CLI has `checkpoint.CreatedAt` / `StartedAt` / `LastInteractionAt` available offline — it can compute real `max(last_checkpoint_ts − first_checkpoint_ts)` per session. Render:

```
Peak session span   1h 03m      (first → last checkpoint timestamp)
```

And optionally, for parity:

```
Continuity (FE)     1.3h        (max steps × 2 min, legacy estimate)
```

Over time the CLI's honest number pressures the FE to adopt the real one, or we bring both under a single server-side definition.

**B) Upstream a fix.** File a small api/FE change to add `session_span_ms = MAX(cp_ts) − MIN(cp_ts)` per session in the existing `/overview/*` data path. This is ~1 SQL change in `api/src/lib/planetscale/repo-overview.ts` plus an FE field swap. Then CLI + FE align permanently on a real metric. I'd scope this as a small PR *before* `entire activity` ships so we don't bake in a second divergent metric.

## 2. Local-first — yes, and the local primitives are already there

You're right, this is a CLI command and the existing `sessions`/`status` model is the template. What I found:

- `strategy.ListSessionStates(ctx)` reads `.git/entire-sessions/*.json` — active session list, offline, fast. Returns `BaseCommit`, `StartedAt`, `LastInteractionAt`, `CheckpointCount`, `Phase`, worktree metadata.
- `strategy.LoadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)` — per-session detail, local.
- `session.NewStateStore(ctx)` — read-only store, no network.
- `manual_commit_logs.go` / `checkpoint.ListCommitted()` — walks the local `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch tree for committed checkpoint metadata.

That gives us, fully local:
- Today's active and just-ended sessions (including un-pushed work the api can't see)
- Committed checkpoints for this repo with timestamps, token counts, files touched, linked-commit SHAs
- Session spans, checkpoint density, streaks, focus areas, linked-commit rate
- Existing `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer lookup via local `git log`

So the v1 architecture should be:

```
entire activity today          → 100% local (no login required)
entire activity --last 7d      → 100% local (this repo)
entire activity --last 30d     → local + api enrichment for server labels (if logged in)
entire activity --repo all     → api-required (cross-repo scope only works there)
entire activity --local-only   → never call api (privacy/offline flag)
```

API calls are **enrichment**, not a dependency. The command works offline. When logged in and online, labels from `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` and cross-repo aggregation become available. If the api is slow or down, CLI degrades gracefully with a small footer: `labels unavailable — offline`.

**Performance budget** also ties to this:
- Local-only paths: <1s for `today`, <3s for `--last 7d`.
- API enrichment is lazy and async: render local data first, fill in label pills as responses arrive (TUI), or batch-fetch before final print (static).
- Cache api responses at `.git/entire-activity-cache/` keyed on checkpoint ID — checkpoint analyses are immutable once computed (pipeline version bump triggers invalidation).

## 3. Three-tier truth table — yes, confirmed native

Three tiers, three sources, each metric tagged at its origin:

| Tier | Source | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Local-authoritative | `.git/entire-sessions/`, local `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch, local `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers | active session list, session span, checkpoint density, streak, linked-commit rate, focus areas, today's un-pushed work |
| Local-derivable | computed from local-authoritative data | sessions/day, checkpoints/day, mode *counts* when we have labels, heatmap cells, top-focus-area rollups |
| Server-authoritative | `api.entire.io` via `api.Client` | LLM-generated `labels[]` per checkpoint, `ToolProfile`, thrashing/bug/architecture flags, cross-repo aggregation, per-user contributor stats |

Each KPI/panel renders a small source hint in the status-bar footer or tooltip (e.g. `labels: server · span: local · linked commits: local`). That's the honesty lever — users know whether a number came from their machine or the cloud.

## Plan changes I'd now make

1. **Local-first architecture** as the explicit default. Add an "Execution Model" section to the plan between "Data Truth Table" and "Core Data Model." Describe the three tiers and how they flow into each view.
2. **Drop the deterministic classifier** (same as before) — but be explicit that labels are server-only enrichment. Sessions without server labels render as unlabeled rather than forcing a local `mixed` that may later disagree with the server.
3. **Replace "Continuity"** — compute real span locally (`last_ts − first_ts`) and surface it as `Peak session span`. Propose upstream api/FE change for consistency; don't replicate the `2 × steps` estimate in the CLI.
4. **Add `--local-only` flag** and document offline degradation.
5. **Caching section**: `.git/entire-activity-cache/<checkpoint-id>.json`, invalidated on `pipeline_version` bump from the api.
6. **Perf budget** written in: today <1s, 7d <3s, 30d <10s, history 90d <30s, all measured on local data with api enrichment async.

3. OK to keep the "no LLM prose" ban in the plan but explicitly clarify that **server-generated labels are not prose** and the CLI renders them as-is (no local re-classification)?

content.text:
Good call on the walkthrough — I found a lot of infrastructure we should ride on rather than build around. Answers in order.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `session.State` already exposes `SessionID`, `BaseCommit`, `WorktreePath`, `StartedAt`, `EndedAt`, `Phase`, `LastInteractionTime`, `StepCount`, `FilesTouched`, `LastCheckpointID` — nearly every field `ActivitySession` needs. The projection is ~10 lines, not a new domain model.
- `strategy.ListSessionStates` and `strategy.ListCheckpoints` are the two data sources. Both already walk the right local stores (`.git/entire-sessions/` and `entire/checkpoints/v1`). Authentication for api enrichment already uses `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient(insecureHTTP)` — the pattern `trail_cmd.go` uses in four places.
- Accessibility infra exists: `NewAccessibleForm`, `ACCESSIBLE=1` env var, `isAccessibleMode()` helper. The accessible mode for `activity` is a fallback renderer that sections the TUI into linear text blocks — not a parallel implementation.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## 1. ActivitySession — concrete projection example

Not a new primitive. A read-only view built in `load.go`:

```go
// cmd/entire/cli/activity/model.go
package activity

import (
    "time"

    "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
    "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
)

// ActivitySession is a read-only projection of a session for activity views.
// It combines local session state, committed checkpoint metadata, and
// (when available) server-fetched labels. It is never persisted.
type ActivitySession struct {
    SessionID       string
    WorktreePath    string
    BaseCommit      string

    StartedAt       time.Time
    LastInteraction time.Time
    EndedAt         *time.Time
    Phase           session.Phase

    CheckpointIDs   []id.CheckpointID
    FilesTouched    []string
    LinkedCommits   []string // SHAs whose message contains this session's Entire-Checkpoint trailers

    // Enrichment (nil when offline or when the server hasn't analyzed the session yet)
    Labels          []string // from api StoredCheckpointAnalysis.extraction.labels; max 3
    ToolProfile     *ToolProfile

    Source          DataSource // local | server | mixed
}

// SpanMinutes returns first→last checkpoint timestamp span.
// Honest time: computed from real timestamps, not an estimate.
// Zero if there are fewer than two checkpoints.
func (a ActivitySession) SpanMinutes() float64 { /* ... */ }

// ActivityCheckpoint is a projection of one checkpoint.
type ActivityCheckpoint struct {
    ID             id.CheckpointID
    SessionID      string
    CreatedAt      time.Time
    FilesTouched   []string
    LinkedCommit   string   // may be empty
    TokenUsage     *agent.TokenUsage
    Labels         []string // from api; empty when offline
    Source         DataSource
}

type DataSource int
const (
    SourceLocal DataSource = iota
    SourceServer
    SourceMixed
)
```

Loader signature:

```go
// cmd/entire/cli/activity/load.go
func LoadActivity(ctx context.Context, opts LoadOpts) (*Activity, error) {
    states, err := strategy.ListSessionStates(ctx)               // local
    committed, err := strategy.ListCheckpoints(ctx)              // local
    linkedMap := lookupLinkedCommits(ctx, committed)             // local git log + trailers
    sessions := project(states, committed, linkedMap)            // pure fn
    if opts.EnrichFromAPI && auth.HasToken() {
        _ = enrichLabels(ctx, sessions)                          // best-effort, async
    }
    return aggregate(sessions), nil
}
```

The projection is pure — no side effects, easy to unit-test with in-memory `session.State` fixtures.

## 2. Why no local classifier — yes, exactly that

Dedup with the server. Rationale:

- The classifier already exists on the api (`api/src/lib/checkpoint-analysis-pipeline.ts`, pipeline version `2026-04-10.v3`), uses the Anthropic SDK to produce `CheckpointExtraction { labels[], blocks[] }` with a canonical 18-label taxonomy, and is what drives the checkpoint summary UI on entire.io.
- A second classifier in the CLI means two implementations, two taxonomies, and drift. Users will see `build` in the TUI and `feature_build` pill in the web app for the same checkpoint — looks like a bug.
- The expensive part (LLM call + transcript analysis) isn't something the CLI wants to do locally anyway. Transcripts aren't always fully resident in the local store for pushed checkpoints.
- Local-cheap signals (`linked commit`, `resumed`, `delegated`, `multi-repo`) stay in the CLI as **badges**, not labels. Those are deterministic facts from local session state, not classifications, and they don't need server round-trips.

Net effect: the CLI consumes labels, renders them, caches them at `.git/entire-activity-cache/<checkpoint-id>.json`, and degrades gracefully to "labels unavailable" when offline. Sessions without server analyses render unlabeled instead of getting a locally-invented label that will later disagree.

## 5. Accessibility — concrete example

Default TUI (dashboard):

```text
┌ Entire Activity ─ today ─ repo: current ─ profile: personal ─ metric: sessions ┐
│ Sessions  3   Checkpoints  11   Linked Commits  2   Active  1   Focus Areas  3 │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

content.text:
Found the relevant infrastructure. Answers in order.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The hackweek PRs already built a `ToolProfile` at `api/src/lib/analysis-queue.ts:336` via `extractToolMetrics()` — it categorizes tool calls into `shell | fileOps | search | mcp | agent | other` using literal tool-name mapping (`Bash → shell`, `Read/Write/Edit → fileOps`, `Grep/Glob → search`, `mcp__* → mcp`, `Agent/Skill → agent`). But it's **counts only, no timing**. The "time spent grepping/conversing/committing" insight does not exist yet.
- Claude Code / Cursor transcripts are JSONL with per-line `timestamp` fields. That's enough to derive tool-time honestly: `duration(tool_use_i) = ts(next tool_use_i+1 or turn_end) − ts(tool_use_i)`. The data is right there — it just needs one new server-side pass.
- "Conversation time" and "commit time" aren't native categories yet. Conversation = assistant-text time between tool calls; commit = bash time matching `^git (commit|push)`. Both are cheap to derive once we're iterating transcripts for timings anyway.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## The tool-time-breakdown idea — let's build it

Current state on the server:

```ts
// api/src/lib/analysis-queue.ts:336 — already exists
extractToolMetrics(sessionsMap): {
  skillsUsed: string[]
  mcpServersUsed: { name, count }[]
  toolProfile: { categories: { shell: {count}, fileOps: {count}, ... }, total }  // counts only
}
```

What the user wants is a **time companion** to `ToolProfile`. I'd propose this be a small follow-on to Alisha's work, scoped as:

### Proposed shape

```ts
// extended — adds durationMs alongside count
toolProfile: {
  categories: {
    shell:        { count: 12, durationMs: 184000 },
    fileOps:      { count: 47, durationMs: 912000 },
    search:       { count: 8,  durationMs: 34000  },   // "grepping"
    mcp:          { count: 3,  durationMs: 19000  },
    agent:        { count: 2,  durationMs: 108000 },
    other:        { count: 1,  durationMs: 4000   },
    conversation: { count: 0,  durationMs: 267000 },   // NEW: assistant text between tool calls
    commit:       { count: 4,  durationMs: 31000  },   // NEW: bash calls matching ^git (commit|push)
  },
  total: { count: 77, durationMs: 1559000 }
}
```

`conversation` and `commit` are virtual categories:
- `conversation` = cumulative gaps where the assistant produced text output between a tool_result and the next tool_use.
- `commit` = sub-category of shell where the bash command matches a commit/push regex — counted *in addition to* shell total so the user sees commit time explicitly without double-counting when summed.

### How the time is computed honestly

Every Claude Code / Cursor transcript line has an ISO-8601 timestamp. For each tool_use content block in an assistant message:

```
duration_i = timestamp(next tool_use OR turn end) − timestamp(tool_use_i)
```

For `conversation`:

```
conv_i = timestamp(next tool_use) − timestamp(tool_result_i)
         only counted when the assistant produced text between them
```

Summing these deltas per category gives the breakdown. The method is transcript-evidence-based — no `2 × steps` estimates. Matches the plan's anti-bullshit stance.

### Where this lives

- **Server, not CLI.** Same reasoning as labels: the CLI shouldn't re-parse transcripts for checkpoints that have already been pushed and analyzed. Extend `extractToolMetrics()` to also emit `durationMs` per category. One PR, small surface change.
- **Schema change** on `StoredCheckpointAnalysis.toolProfile`. Additive (new fields), backward compatible. Old consumers still see counts.
- **For local/active sessions**, the CLI does compute this locally from the live transcript — same algorithm, Go implementation. This is the one place a shared algorithm is worth duplicating, because active session transcripts aren't on the server yet.

### CLI rendering — Agents view

```text
┌ Tool time by agent (last 30d) ────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Claude Code   fileOps 2h 14m · shell 48m · conversation 1h 02m        │
│               search 22m · agent 18m · mcp 4m                         │
│               of which committing: 6m (11 commits)                    │
│                                                                         │
│ Codex         fileOps 38m · shell 14m · conversation 24m              │
│               search 4m · agent 0 · mcp 0                             │
│               of which committing: 2m (3 commits)                     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Per-session drill-down renders the same breakdown for the selected session. Range/history views sum across sessions.

### What to call out honestly

- **Tool duration** is the wall-clock gap in the transcript, which includes the agent's thinking plus the tool's actual execution time. It is not pure execution time. The plan should label it `Time between tool calls` or `Session time by category` — not "execution time."
- **`conversation`** specifically captures response-writing + thinking time. It's probably the largest bucket for well-behaved sessions, and that's fine — users will find it informative.
- Agents that don't emit timestamps (some future agent) would return empty timings. Conditional metric, same as tokens.

### Tradeoff

If we don't want to touch the api for v1, alternative: compute tool-time locally from transcripts we have resident (active + recently committed). Downsides: for committed checkpoints the CLI has to pull transcript blobs from the `entire/checkpoints/v1` tree, which is slow for range/history views; and we'd have the same local-vs-server drift risk we're trying to avoid for labels. I'd push the change to the server.

## On #3 — the `schema_version` field

You're right to question it. It's preference + future-proofing, not a feature users invoke.

**What it is**: a single field at the top of `--json` output:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "v1",
  "generated_at": "2026-04-16T14:23:11Z",
  "scope": { "repo": "entireio/cli", "from": "2026-04-09", "to": "2026-04-16" },
  "sessions": [ ... ],
  "aggregates": { ... }
}
```

**Why it earns its keep**:
- Once someone pipes `entire activity --json` into a script or cron (standup bot, dashboard, another CLI), our output shape becomes an implicit contract. Rename a field in v2 and their script silently breaks.
- With a version field, consumers gate on it (`if schema_version !== "v1" warn-or-bail`), and we can evolve the format without tiptoeing.
- Cost: ~20 bytes per JSON output. Adds no complexity to the producer.

**When it's not worth it**: if we declare `--json` output internal/unstable for v1 and documentation says "shape may change," skip the field. That's a reasonable call. I lean toward including it because once users start scripting against it (day 1), we've lost the option of declaring it unstable.

**Accessibility**: the field is just in the JSON — user sees it any time they run `--json`. Not tied to a specific subcommand, not hidden behind a flag.

## On the numbering

You're right — accessibility was #5 in my callout list, not #3. My prior message numbered them 1-7 in the first "other callouts" section, and accessibility was #5. I'll keep the numbering consistent going forward.

## What lands in the plan doc

- **New section: "Agent Insights — Tool Time Breakdown"** under the Agents view. Specifies the 8 categories (6 existing + conversation + commit), honest time definition, server-side derivation, and CLI rendering.
- **Upstream dependency**: extend `extractToolMetrics()` to also emit `durationMs`. Same PR that adds `session_span_ms`. Both land before `entire activity` ships.
- **Decision on `schema_version`**: include it as `"v1"`. Footnote the rationale.

Anything you'd add/cut to the 8 categories before I write it up? Specifically:
- Is `conversation` the right name, or do you prefer `thinking` / `writing` / `prose`?
- Is the `commit` sub-bucket useful at the category level, or just as an aggregate stat ("committed 11 times, ~6m total")?
- Anything else explicit you want (e.g., time in `Skill` invocations called out separately, time-per-agent-subagent for Task delegations)?

`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (if subagents available) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in plan (not "add validation")
- Exact commands with expected output
- Reference relevant skills with @ syntax
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Plan Review Loop

After completing each chunk of the plan:

1. Dispatch plan-document-reviewer subagent (see plan-document-reviewer-prompt.md) with precisely crafted review context — never your session history. This keeps the reviewer focused on the plan, not your thought process.
   - Provide: chunk content, path to spec document
2. If ❌ Issues Found:
   - Fix the issues in the chunk
   - Re-dispatch reviewer for that chunk
   - Repeat until ✅ Approved
3. If ✅ Approved: proceed to next chunk (or execution handoff if last chunk)

**Chunk boundaries:** Use `## Chunk N: <name>` headings to delimit chunks. Each chunk should be ≤1000 lines and logically self-contained.

**Review loop guidance:**
- Same agent that wrote the plan fixes it (preserves context)
- If loop exceeds 5 iterations, surface to human for guidance
- Reviewers are advisory - explain disagreements if you believe feedback is incorrect

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Ready to execute?"**

**Execution path depends on harness capabilities:**

**If harness has subagents (Claude Code, etc.):**
- **REQUIRED:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Do NOT offer a choice - subagent-driven is the standard approach
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If harness does NOT have subagents:**
- Execute plan in current session using superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

# Entire Activity Design

Date: 2026-04-15 (revised 2026-04-16)

## Summary

`entire activity` is a new read-only product surface for understanding work captured by Entire over time.

It is centered on:

- **sessions** as the primary unit of work
- **checkpoints** as the evidence trail inside a session
- **repo, time, and agent** as first-class grouping dimensions

This is not a sprint tool and should not use sprint language. It is an Entire-native activity layer over existing session, checkpoint, transcript, and commit-linkage data — rendered as a tabbed dashboard in the terminal.

## Goals

- Show what happened today and across selectable time ranges.
- Make checkpoint and session activity easy to scan quickly.
- Surface useful, defensible insights instead of generic churn metrics.
- Support today / range / history / agents / repos / report tabs in v1.
- Support interactive TUI and static output in v1.
- Use only metrics that are directly available now or safely derivable from existing data.
- Reuse existing CLI infrastructure (session state, checkpoint store, auth, lipgloss styles) rather than duplicating it.

## Non-Goals

- No productivity score.
- No “most modified files” leaderboard as a primary signal.
- No sprint framing.
- No LLM-generated prose in the CLI. (Server-side LLM classification is consumed as data, not re-generated locally.)
- No claims of labor time or focus time beyond actual timestamp spans.
- No local reimplementation of the server-side checkpoint analysis pipeline.

## Product Definition

`entire activity` answers:

- what happened
- when it happened
- where it happened
- what kind of work it was
- which agents and models were involved
- which checkpoints linked to commits
- what should likely be resumed or finished

## Information Architecture

The v1 surface is a **tabbed dashboard**. Six top-level tabs:

```
today │ range │ history │ agents │ repos │ report
```

Rules:

- Each tab is a self-contained view with its own panel layout. Panels never span tabs.
- Active tab is visually distinct (amber `214` with an underline rule); inactive tabs are faint gray `244`.
- Keyboard: `1-6` jump directly to a tab. `tab` / `shift-tab` cycle. `q` quits.
- Within a tab, arrow keys move between panels/rows. `enter` opens drill-down. `esc` closes drill-down.
- CLI subcommands map 1:1 to tabs: `entire activity today` opens the today tab, `entire activity agents` opens agents tab, etc.

Profiles only change defaults and emphasis (heatmap metric, whether token panels are prominent, etc.):

- `personal` (default)
- `team`
- `observability`

## Command Surface

```bash
entire activity                                 # opens TUI on 'today' tab
entire activity today
entire activity range --last 7d
entire activity range --from 2026-04-01 --to 2026-04-15
entire activity history
entire activity agents
entire activity repos
entire activity report --template daily --format markdown
```

Shared flags:

```bash
--repo current|owner/name|all|local
--profile personal|team|observability
--from YYYY-MM-DD
--to YYYY-MM-DD
--last 7d|14d|30d
--group-by repo|day|agent
--view cards|table
--json
--local-only    # never call the api; labels unavailable
--no-color      # also honors NO_COLOR env var
```

Notes:

- `entire activity` (no args) opens the TUI on the `today` tab.
- `--repo all` is the default for logged-in users and covers every repo the user has api access to. `--repo current` narrows to the current worktree's repo. `--repo local` forces offline / this-repo-only mode.
- All subcommands support static terminal output and JSON output.
- `--json` output always includes `"schema_version": "v1"` at the top level.

## Execution Model

### Local-first, api-enriched

- **Local is the default data source.** `entire activity today` with no login returns a complete, honest view of the current repo's activity using only local data.
- **API enrichment is lazy.** When `entire login` has produced a token, the CLI fetches server-authoritative labels and tool-time data per checkpoint. Enrichment fills in asynchronously in the TUI and is batched before final print in static mode.
- **Offline / not-logged-in fallback** is silent. Tab chrome shows a single line: `labels: offline · tip: run 'entire login' for agent insights`.
- **Performance budget:**
  - `today`: < 1s local, < 2s with api enrichment
  - `range --last 7d`: < 3s local, < 6s with enrichment
  - `range --last 30d`: < 6s local, < 12s with enrichment
  - `history` (90d): < 10s local, < 30s with enrichment
- **Cache** at `.git/entire-activity-cache/<checkpoint-id>.json` for api responses. Invalidated when `StoredCheckpointAnalysis.pipeline_version` changes.

### Three-tier Data Truth Table

Every metric is sourced from exactly one tier. The UI tags metrics with their tier via the tab chrome footer (e.g. `labels: server · span: local · linked commits: local`).

#### Tier 1 — Local-authoritative

Readable from `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json` (session state) and `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch (committed metadata):

- session ID, checkpoint ID
- session started / ended / last-interaction timestamps
- session phase, step count
- checkpoint timestamps
- files touched per session / per checkpoint
- base commit, worktree path, worktree ID
- agent type, model name (when state records it)
- token usage (when the agent or hook reports it)
- prompt text (scoped per checkpoint)
- attribution metadata (`InitialAttribution`)
- `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer presence on user commits (via local `git log`)
- hook-provided session metrics (`SessionMetrics.DurationMs/TurnCount/ContextTokens`) for agents that emit them (e.g., Cursor)

#### Tier 2 — Local-derivable

Cheap computation from tier 1 with no api call:

- **session span minutes** = `last_checkpoint_ts − first_checkpoint_ts` (honest first-to-last timestamp, replaces the FE `max(steps) × 2 / 60` estimate)
- checkpoints per session, checkpoint density, median checkpoint gap
- sessions/day, checkpoints/day
- active day count, streaks (same algorithm as FE `useUserDashboardData.ts`)
- heatmap cell intensity
- intra-day hour buckets
- resume-after-gap detection
- focus area assignment from `files_touched` via rule engine
- linked commit count, linked commit rate (via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer lookup)
- commit-linked vs exploratory-only split
- badges (`resumed`, `linked commit`, `delegated`, `multi-repo`)
- active-session rollups (un-pushed work that only exists locally)

#### Tier 3 — Server-authoritative

Requires `entire login` and a network round trip. Fetched per committed checkpoint and cached:

- **work-mode labels** — `CheckpointExtraction.labels[]` from `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` (18-value multi-label taxonomy, max 3 per checkpoint)
- **`toolProfile.categories[*].count`** — tool usage counts (shell / fileOps / search / mcp / agent / other)
- **`toolProfile.categories[*].durationMs`** — tool time per category (**pending upstream server change**, see Upstream Dependencies)
- `skillsUsed`, `mcpServersUsed`, `modelsUsed`, `agentsUsed`
- execution feedback: `thrashing`, `bugProfile`, `architectureChanges`
- cross-repo aggregation for `--repo all`
- session span canonicalization (**pending** — until then CLI uses tier 2)

## Core Data Model

Activity types are **read-only projections**, not new primitives. They are built in `load.go` from existing `session.State` + `checkpoint.CheckpointSummary` + `checkpoint.CommittedMetadata` (+ optional api `StoredCheckpointAnalysis`). They are never persisted. The existing `session` and `checkpoint` packages remain the canonical owners of underlying data.

### ActivitySession

Projected from `session.State` + per-session checkpoint rollups. Key fields:

- repo, session ID, branch (when available), worktree ID, worktree path
- started at, ended at, last interaction at
- span minutes (tier 2: honest, first→last checkpoint)
- step count, task checkpoint count
- checkpoints: `[]ActivityCheckpoint`
- agents used, models used
- focus areas (tier 2, from `files_touched`)
- labels (tier 3, from api; empty when offline)
- badges (tier 2, deterministic local)
- token totals (tier 1 when available)
- linked commit SHAs (tier 2)
- is active, is resumable
- `source` (local | server | mixed)

### ActivityCheckpoint

Projected from `checkpoint.CheckpointSummary` + `checkpoint.CommittedMetadata` (+ optional api). Key fields:

- repo, session ID, checkpoint ID
- timestamp
- is task checkpoint, tool use ID
- agent, model
- focus areas (tier 2)
- linked commit SHA (tier 2)
- token usage (tier 1 when available)
- turn ID
- labels (tier 3, from api; empty when offline)
- tool profile (tier 3, from api; empty when offline)
- badges (tier 2)
- source

### ActivityDay

Per-day rollup. Key fields: date, repos, sessions, checkpoints, task checkpoints, linked commits, token totals, label counts, focus area counts, resume count, tool-time totals (tier 3).

### ActivityRangeSummary

Range-level aggregates. Fields include: from, to, repos touched, sessions, checkpoints, task checkpoints, linked commits, active days, tokens, label counts (with confidence gating, see below), focus area counts, agent counts, model counts, repo summaries, top sessions, tool-time totals.

### ActivityRepoSummary / ActivityAgentSummary

Repo- and agent-scoped rollups used in `repos` and `agents` tabs.

## Labels — Server-Authoritative

### Why No Local Classifier

The entire.io api already runs `checkpoint-analysis-pipeline.ts` (pipeline version `2026-04-10.v3`) which uses the Anthropic SDK to produce `CheckpointExtraction { labels[], blocks[] }`. Results are stored as `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` in the db. This is the same pipeline that drives the web app's checkpoint summary UI (PR #1021).

A second classifier in the CLI would produce a different taxonomy, different weights, and eventual drift. Users would see `build` in the TUI and `feature_build` in the web app for the same checkpoint — a reportable bug. We avoid that by letting the server own classification and having the CLI consume and render.

### Canonical Taxonomy

Labels are multi-label with max 3 per checkpoint, drawn from `CHECKPOINT_LABELS` in `api/src/types.ts`:

```
feature_build, bug_fix, refactor, performance, optimization,
investigation, configuration, testing, deployment, recovery,
planning, security_fix, documentation, migration, telemetry,
observability, enhancement, dependencies
```

### Rendering

- Session cards and checkpoint rows show up to 3 label pills (semantic color per label; see Visual Language).
- Sessions without a server analysis render **unlabeled**, not as `mixed`. Offline mode suppresses label pills entirely and notes it in the chrome footer.
- Range-level "modes" panels aggregate by summing label occurrences across checkpoints/sessions.
- A range never claims a dominant mode unless: top label share ≥ 0.55 and top leads runner-up by ≥ 0.15. Otherwise render `Modes: feature_build 4 · bug_fix 3 · testing 2`.

## Badges — Local Deterministic

Badges are cheap local facts, not classifications. They don't require the api.

- `⚑ linked` — session has at least one `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer on an active-branch commit
- `↻ resumed` — session started after ≥ 6h gap from the prior session on the same branch
- `⇢ delegated` — session has task checkpoint count ≥ 1
- `◎ multi-repo` — session spans multiple repos (only available with `--repo all`)
- `● active` — session phase is `ACTIVE` or `IDLE` with `EndedAt == nil`
- `✓ committed` — checkpoint has a linked commit

## Tool Time — Agent Insights

Tool-time breakdown is the primary metric on the `agents` tab. It answers "how much time did the agent spend grepping vs conversing vs committing."

### Categories

8 categories, semantically colored:

| Category | Mapping rule | Color (256) |
|---|---|---|
| `shell` | `Bash` | `179` |
| `fileOps` | `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | `75` |
| `search` | `Grep`, `Glob` | `81` |
| `mcp` | `mcp__*` | `170` |
| `agent` | `Agent`, `Skill` | `99` |
| `other` | everything else | `244` |
| `conversation` | assistant text time between tool_result and next tool_use | `250` |
| `commit` | `Bash` where command matches `^git (commit\|push)` | `220` |

`conversation` and `commit` are virtual categories:

- `conversation` is a **sum of gaps** where the assistant produced text between a `tool_result` and the next `tool_use`. It does not overlap with any other category.
- `commit` is a **sub-bucket of shell**. Rendered as a secondary line under shell and summed separately ("of which committing: 6m"); not double-counted when categories are summed.

### Derivation

For each assistant message containing `tool_use` content blocks, measure timestamps from the transcript JSONL:

```
duration(tool_use_i) = timestamp(next tool_use OR turn end) − timestamp(tool_use_i)
```

For `conversation`:

```
conversation_i = timestamp(next tool_use) − timestamp(tool_result_i)
                  counted only when assistant text was produced in the gap
```

### Where Computation Lives

- **For committed checkpoints** (tier 3): computed server-side by extending `extractToolMetrics` in `api/src/lib/analysis-queue.ts`. CLI consumes `toolProfile.categories[*].durationMs` from the api.
- **For active / un-pushed sessions** (tier 2): computed locally in the CLI by parsing the live transcript. Same algorithm, Go implementation, so the CLI can show tool-time for today's work before it's pushed.

Honest labels: the UI calls this "Time between tool calls" or "Session time by category." Not "execution time" — it includes agent thinking.

## Focus Areas

Focus areas are a required product signal. They determine which work clusters the user is spending time on.

### Rule Source

Resolution order:

1. repo-local config (`.entire/activity_areas.json`)
2. built-in rules (shipped with the CLI)
3. fallback path clustering (first meaningful repo-relative directory boundary)

Repo-local config schema:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "areas": [
    { "match": "cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/**", "label": "checkpoint storage", "priority": 100 }
  ]
}
```

### Matching Rules

- highest priority wins
- ties broken by longest match
- fallback to first meaningful repo-relative directory boundary if no rule matches

### Built-In Default Rules

For this repo (entireio/cli):

- `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/**` → `checkpoint storage`
- `cmd/entire/cli/session/**` → `session state`
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/**` → `checkpoint strategy`
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/**` → `agent integrations`
- `cmd/entire/cli/search**` → `search`
- `cmd/entire/cli/explain**` → `explain`
- `cmd/entire/cli/status**` → `status`
- `cmd/entire/cli/activity/**` → `activity`
- `cmd/entire/cli/trail/**` → `trails`
- `cmd/entire/cli/hooks**` → `hooks`
- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/**` → `integration tests`
- `e2e/**` → `e2e`
- `docs/architecture/**` → `architecture docs`
- `docs/**` → `docs`

### Area Ranking

Do not rank by file count.

Session area score:

- `4 × checkpoint_participation`
- `+1` if area appears in 2+ consecutive checkpoints
- `+1` if area appears in a linked-commit session

Range area score:

- `3 × session_participation`
- `3 × checkpoint_participation`
- `+1` if area appears across multiple repos (only with `--repo all`)

Render only top 1–3 focus areas in summary surfaces.

These are **optional enrichment** — v1 ships without them. CLI handles absence gracefully. File as separate PR on entire.io:
